app.title: SwissCareerScore
app.tagline: Compare Swiss occupations and education paths on official data — with your own weights.

disclaimer.long: Scores combine official Swiss statistics with documented estimates. They describe averages of broad occupation groups, not your personal prospects. Use them to ask better questions — talk to a career counsellor (berufsberatung.ch) before deciding.

pay.name: Pay
pay.desc: Median gross monthly wage, weighted 35 % entry level and 65 % mid-career.

stability.name: Job stability
stability.desc: Low registered unemployment in the occupation.

demand.name: Demand
demand.desc: Share of employers that find it hard to recruit at this level in this sector.

aiResilience.name: AI resilience
aiResilience.desc: Low exposure of the occupation's tasks to AI and automation (estimate).

trainingEase.name: Training ease
trainingEase.desc: High share of learners who complete the training.

entryAccess.name: Easy entry
entryAccess.desc: Low admission hurdles (numerus clausus, aptitude tests, limited places).

timeToQualify.name: Fast start
timeToQualify.desc: Few years from the end of compulsory school to qualification.

careerGrowth.name: Career growth
careerGrowth.desc: Wage progression from under 30 to over 50 in the occupation group.

workLifeBalance.name: Work-life balance
workLifeBalance.desc: Little night work and moderate usual weekly hours.

flexibility.name: Remote / flexibility
flexibility.desc: Share of people in the sector who work from home at least occasionally.

mobility.name: International mobility
mobility.desc: Recognition abroad, language independence and transferability (rubric).

regional.name: Regional availability
regional.desc: Available in many regions and language areas (rubric).

meaning.name: Meaning / societal value
meaning.desc: No defensible Swiss per-occupation source yet — off by default.

weights.title: What matters to you?
weights.presetHelp: Balanced = equal weights (see methodology). Moving any slider switches to Custom.
weights.overlap: {a} and {b} move together (ρ = {rho}). Weighting both counts a similar signal twice.

filters.title: Filters
filters.hint: Filters only hide entries; scores and ranks stay comparable.

list.results: {count, plural, =0 {No results} one {# result} other {# results}}
list.insufficientTip: Less than 60 % of your weights are backed by data. Shown without rank.
list.fragileTip: Rank moves by up to {shift} places if any single weight changes by ±20 %.
list.pool: Occupations and education paths are ranked separately (percentiles within each group).

entity.breakdownHelp: Each bar shows weight × dimension score. Missing dimensions are dropped and their weight is redistributed.
entity.radarDesc: Dimension scores from 0 (worst in group) to 100 (best in group).
entity.dataHelp: Click any value to see its source, year and confidence.
entity.sensitivityHelp: Largest rank change when one weight is changed by ±20 %.

inputs.telework: Works from home at least occasionally

source.title: Source
source.missing: No data — this value is missing and is not imputed.

compare.title: Compare
compare.empty: Select up to 4 entries in the ranking to compare them side by side.

ahp.title: What matters more?
ahp.desc: Answer a few pairwise questions. We derive weights with the Analytic Hierarchy Process (AHP).
ahp.question: Which matters more to you?
ahp.inconsistent: Your answers contradict each other somewhat (CR > 0.10). Consider revisiting them.

groups.effort: Low effort to qualify (training ease, easy entry, fast start)

share.help: Your settings are stored in the URL — share or bookmark it.
